newsitem.title: UK: New sleaze allegations hit UK Tories - paper.
newsitem.headline: New sleaze allegations hit UK Tories - paper.

text.p: A Conservative election agent secretly plotted to finance a Green Party candidate to strip votes from Labour in a marginal British seat, the Observer newspaper reported on Sunday.
In a taped conversation last week, the agent promised to send a cash-filled envelope to pay the candidate's deposit, said the paper.

"An Observer investigation can reveal that Robin Meads, a Tory agent and constituency chairman, arranged the undercover payment to persuade the Greens to field a candidate in the closely contested seat of Lincoln. Yesterday he resigned after he was confronted with our evidence," said the paper.
Lincoln is the 15th most marginal Conservative seat.

The paper said that when confronted with the allegations, 52-year-old Meads said: "We have been discussing whether there should be a Green candidate with them. I said there might be people in the Conservative Party who had Green interests."
In his resignation statement, Meads said he acted alone and was resigning because he did not want his actions to distract people from the "real issues of this campaign".
The Conservative candidate Tony Brown was quoted by the paper as saying he knew about his agent's scheme.
"I was aware that he had been having discussions with the Green Party although I was not aware of the detail," the paper quoted him as saying. "It was not my idea."

The Conservatives have struggled to shake off sleaze allegations at the outset of their campaign to win power in the May 1 election, with a so-called "cash-for-questions" scandal and allegations of sexual wrongdoing swamping the political agenda.
